key_insight: Hodge–de Rham PINNs augment standard PINNs with topology-aware 1-form representations to address failures on PDE domains containing holes, punctures, or voids.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets PDE modeling where circulation, path dependence, and nontrivial topology can undermine conventional scalar-potential PINNs.
method: Parameterize a 1-form using the Hodge–Morrey–Friedrichs decomposition.
Train with an associated PDE loss and connect the learned form to scalar solutions through integral operators.
Use exhaustion functions when the loss integrability condition is not satisfied.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical guarantees and experiments on topologically adverse problems, including the Aharonov–Bohm effect, but provides no quantitative results.
watch_item: Connecting the 1-form PDE to the scalar-potential problem can require nontrivial integration and case-specific operator derivations.
paper_title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
